title: Scalar compatibility of the smooth exceptional composition comparison
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^a}$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, and use the rational constructible categories $\mathcal C_E(W)=D^b_c(W,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], the derived pullbacks and exceptional inverse images of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and the exact scalar extensions $T_W=T_{L/E,W}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Write $G_{h,E}=Rh_E^!$ and $H_{h,E}=Lh_E^*(-)(d_h)[2d_h]$ for a smooth separated $h$ of pure relative dimension $d_h$. Let $\gamma_{h,E}:H_{h,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,E}$ be the rationalization of the simultaneous integral purity family of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], as in [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. Denote by $b_{h,K}:T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}G_{h,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,L}T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}K$ the rationalized counit-normalized comparison specified in that integral scalar-naturality statement.

Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $K\in\mathcal C_E(Z)$. Then $gf$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d+e$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], so $b_{gf,K}$ is defined. For $R=E,L$, let $c^R_{g,f}:G_{gf,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f,R}G_{g,R}$ be the canonical exceptional composition comparison transported from the integral comparison in [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence], with the direction of [thm-pur-composition-coherence]. Put
$$\beta_{g,f,K}=G_{f,L}(b_{g,K})\circ b_{f,G_{g,E}K}:T_XG_{f,E}G_{g,E}K\longrightarrow G_{f,L}G_{g,L}T_ZK.$$
Then the actual composition comparisons satisfy the scalar equation
$$\beta_{g,f,K}\circ T_X(c^E_{g,f,K})=c^L_{g,f,T_ZK}\circ b_{gf,K}.$$
This is an equality of natural transformations in $K$, with the unit, successive coefficient-extension and shift identifications specified by the scalar comparisons above.

proof.text: For $R=E,L$, put $u^R_K:H_{gf,R}K\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{f,R}H_{g,R}K$ for the canonical pullback/twist/shift comparison, and $q^R_K=\gamma_{f,R,G_{g,R}K}H_{f,R}(\gamma_{g,R,K})$. Apply [lem-pur-rational-normalized-purity-diagrams]. It verifies all lattice and uniform finite-Tor domains and gives $c^R_K\gamma_{gf,R,K}=q^R_Ku^R_K$ for the actual specified compositor, as well as $b_{h,M}T(\gamma_{h,E,M})=\gamma_{h,L,TM}a_{h,M}$ for $h=f,g,gf$. All maps are natural, with their specified unit, coefficient-associator and shift identifications.

proof.text: Set $A_K=H_{f,L}(a_{g,K})a_{f,H_{g,E}K}$. By [lem-pur-iterated-purity-scalar-pasting], the canonical twisted-pullback compositor satisfies $A_KT_X(u^E_K)=u^L_{T_ZK}a_{gf,K}$, and horizontal pasting gives $\beta_KT_X(q^E_K)=q^L_{T_ZK}A_K$. The lemma includes the ordered twist factors, even shifts, and the naturality moves for the two purity squares; these equations use the same comparisons as Step 1.

source.place: Composition-coherence transport paragraph; unit sk-thm-purity-transport Step 3

proof.text:
Precompose both proposed maps $T_XG_{gf,E}K\to G_{f,L}G_{g,L}T_ZK$ with the isomorphism $T_X(\gamma_{gf,E,K})$. The equations of [lem-pur-rational-normalized-purity-diagrams] and [lem-pur-iterated-purity-scalar-pasting] give
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_KT_X(c^E_K)T_X(\gamma_{gf,E,K})
&=\beta_KT_X(q^E_K)T_X(u^E_K)\\
&=q^L_{T_ZK}A_KT_X(u^E_K)
=q^L_{T_ZK}u^L_{T_ZK}a_{gf,K},\\
c^L_{T_ZK}b_{gf,K}T_X(\gamma_{gf,E,K})
&=c^L_{T_ZK}\gamma_{gf,L,T_ZK}a_{gf,K}
=q^L_{T_ZK}u^L_{T_ZK}a_{gf,K}.
\end{aligned}$$
Cancel the common precomposition isomorphism. Since all factors are natural, component equality gives the claimed equality of natural transformations. The two cited lemmas assert these very equations with the specified identity-extension, successive-extension associators and shift comparisons. Substituting those equations into the displayed chains gives identical ordered factors on the two routes, and the same cancellation gives the required identifications.
